missionPremise: Bastrop's zoning cell reads 99.77% satisfied-present off a cell carrying its ENVELOPE facet's measurement; the stamp really measures 15.22% (9,642 of 63,357). The planner's falsifiable hypothesis, offered as NOT evidence: 15.22% is not a coverage failure but the wrong denominator, because unincorporated Texas has no municipal zoning authority and nothing to stamp, so the corrected figure might land near 100% and need no remediation. Source: _dispatches/2026-08-19_ss-w15_dispatch.md, OPS-16 amendment A-020 ruled 2026-08-19.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (a) read the measured incorporated-parcel share of Bastrop and the stamped share of THAT set, each with its counting rule; (b) see the denominator DECLARED into SS-W12's scorer capability rather than built as a fourth one-off scorer; (c) tell a county MEASURED BELOW BAR from one NEVER MEASURED on the console without reading source; (d) re-run every figure here from a checked-in instrument.
scopeBasis: The zoning denominator and the display class it forces. Deliberately excluded, each with a reason: running --apply against the live ledger (not this lane's to run, and it moves the Texas launch-gate arithmetic); merging or deploying; the six unspecified rail scorers (SS-W12/SS-W14 own their specs); re-wiring city zoning layers (an acquisition job, not a measurement job); the envelope facet's denominator (its conjunction measures whether an envelope can be DERIVED, which is legitimately a county-wide question, so its county denominator is correct for its own question); retiring or re-denominating countyCoverageScoreCli.ts (another lane's file, and an operator ruling).

verdictOnTheHypothesis.falsified: The 'near 100%, remediation is nothing' branch is FALSE. Bastrop measures 79.60%, not ~100%, and the remediation is not nothing.
verdictOnTheHypothesis.whatTheShortfallActuallyIs: One named city. Smithville: 2,397 incorporated parcels, 0 stamped, 20.03% of the incorporated denominator on its own. It is the eCode360 city, structurally deferred since 2026-05-19 and re-ruled 2026-08-04 to a scrape posture. The corrected denominator did not erase the gap; it named it, and turned a number that read as systemic failure into one already-owned acquisition item.

operatorRulingsRequested.severity: HIGH, blocks any --apply of the zoning rail
operatorRulingsRequested.question: Which instrument owns facet 'zoning'?
operatorRulingsRequested.detail: TWO checked-in instruments now write it with DIFFERENT denominators. countyCoverageScoreCli.ts (lane SS-W13's file) uses the county parcel count; countyRailScoreCli.ts uses the incorporated count. Both upsert the same (county_fips, facet) primary key, so the last one run wins the cell: on Bastrop that is 15.22% versus 79.60% depending on which CLI ran most recently. This is a paired-control divergence I created deliberately and named rather than resolved, because retiring or re-denominating a live instrument in another lane's file is an operator ruling (DEV_PROCESS 5.4). It is written into the registry's zoning note so it cannot be found by accident. Neither instrument was applied.
operatorRulingsRequested.recommendation: Retire the zoning and envelope facets from countyCoverageScoreCli.ts and let the rail-scoring capability own them, which is the direction P-47 exists to move in: twelve writers and three scorers becomes one declared capability. Do it as its own change with SS-W13's file owner, not inside this PR.

operatorRulingsRequested.severity: MEDIUM, changes what the ledger says about Texas
operatorRulingsRequested.question: Apply the corrected zoning rule to the live ledger, and when?
operatorRulingsRequested.detail: Nothing here moved a cell. Applying moves nine cells: Bastrop's zoning cell from a wrong 99.77% satisfied-present to a measured 79.60% measured-below-bar, and eight others onto the corrected denominator. It also REMOVES the basis for 243 counties' zoning rows if any exist, because those counties are now refused rather than scored. The Texas completeness arithmetic does not move from the DISPLAY split (proven), but it does move if a cell that read satisfied-present stops reading it.
operatorRulingsRequested.recommendation: Apply only after R1 is ruled, or the next run of the other CLI silently reverts it.
